summary: Learn biodiversity management and nature positive strategy with TNFD, GRI 304, and mitigation hierarchy tools. Build practical action plans.
lede: Biodiversity management and nature positive strategy provides a practical method for assessing nature-related impacts and dependencies, prioritising habitats, and designing actions that follow the mitigation hierarchy. You will work with baseline assessments, stakeholder mapping, biodiversity risk registers, and restoration planning to support project and land-use decisions. The course also develops practical reporting skills through TNFD LEAP screening, nature-positive scorecards, KPI tracking, and applied templates. It introduces the Global Biodiversity Framework and science-based targets for nature at an overview level, helping you create usable evidence for disclosures, approvals, and investment decisions despite data gaps and competing priorities.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals working at the point where biodiversity, project delivery, and reporting intersect. You may be building assessments, advising on mitigation, preparing disclosures, or coordinating actions across technical and non-technical teams. Sustainability Managers who need biodiversity actions linked to ESG delivery. Environmental Consultants who assess habitat impacts and mitigation options. Biodiversity Officers who prepare risk screens and conservation measures. ESG Analysts who support TNFD-aligned nature-related disclosure. Natural Resource Planners who manage land-use and ecological trade-offs. Project Managers who coordinate biodiversity inputs for delivery decisions. Environmental Compliance Officers who track nature-related commitments. Restoration Specialists who design site recovery and habitat interventions. Corporate Reporting Managers who compile biodiversity evidence for leadership. Procurement and Supply Chain Specialists who assess biodiversity hotspots.
prerequisites: You should bring a basic understanding of environmental or sustainability concepts, plus experience in projects, reporting, planning, or operations. A laptop is recommended for exercises using templates, mapping screenshots, and dashboard-style outputs, and having a live or recent project case will make the practical work more valuable.
